scenarios.title: Acoustic bridge crack correlation in lab beams
scenarios.manuscript_excerpt:
Title: Low-Cost Acoustic Attenuation Observations in Prestressed Concrete Lab Beams
Authors: Yugyung Lee, Alex Rivera
Abstract: A critical bottleneck and unsolved problem is that structural concrete cracking degrades highway infrastructure over decades of cyclic traffic loading. In this laboratory note we report an unexpected 14 dB acoustic attenuation shift across micro-cracks in three prestressed concrete beams under four-point bending in our structures lab. Further theoretical modeling is needed to understand wave dispersion across aggregate boundaries.
Keywords: acoustic sensing; concrete beams; wave attenuation; structural mechanics

scenarios.title: Biomarker expression change in cell culture

Title: Hypoxia-Induced Upregulation of Transcriptomic Marker-Z in Cultured Endothelial Cells
Authors: Mei Lin, Jordan Patel
Abstract: A critical bottleneck and unsolved problem is that cellular responses to acute oxygen deprivation remain incompletely characterized in microvascular tissue models. Transcriptomic profiling of 48 multi-well plates showed a reproducible two-fold upregulation of Marker-Z after six hours of hypoxia exposure in vitro. We have not yet identified a clinical diagnostic platform or therapeutic inhibitor target.
Keywords: transcriptomics; hypoxia; endothelial cells; biomarker discovery

Title: Grain Boundary Density Variations in Spin-Coated Halide Perovskite Thin Films
Authors: Priya Nair, Samuel Cho
Abstract: A critical bottleneck and unsolved problem is that crystalline morphology strongly influences charge carrier lifetime in solution-processed semiconductors. Varying thermal annealing time between 10 and 45 minutes at 110 C systematically altered grain boundary density in spin-coated halide perovskite films on glass substrates. Additional stability characterization under ambient humidity is planned.
Keywords: perovskite thin films; thermal annealing; grain boundaries; photovoltaics

scenarios.title: Graph spectral clustering bound on synthetic networks

Title: Tighter Eigenvalue Gap Bounds for Spectral Partitioning on Random Regular Graphs
Authors: David Kim, Elena Rostova
Abstract: A critical bottleneck and unsolved problem is that spectral graph partitioning relies on concentration bounds for the second eigenvalue of the normalized Laplacian matrix. In this theoretical manuscript we prove a tighter eigenvalue gap bound for random regular graphs with degree d >= 6 compared with classical Cheeger bounds using trace method expansions. No empirical benchmark or software implementation has been constructed yet.
Keywords: spectral graph theory; eigenvalue gap; random regular graphs; combinatorics

Abstract: A critical bottleneck and unsolved problem is that root-associated microbial communities shift rapidly during prolonged agricultural drought periods. 16S rRNA metagenomic sequencing of 12 greenhouse pots revealed consistent enrichment of two rhizosphere bacterial taxa during a 21-day water restriction protocol in loam soil. Field inoculant formulations have not yet been explored.
Keywords: soil microbiome; drought stress; metagenomics; rhizosphere bacteria
